À fruit smoothie is not a good way to eat your fruit. Why? Because when we smoothie fruit, the blending process pulverizes the fiber in them (metal blades in a blender are very intense, way way more powerful than our teeth). Aren’t fruit natural and good for us? Well, the thing is- all the fruit you find today have been bred for many centuries to be extra sweet. So even a whole piece of fruit contains much more sugar than it’s ancestral version. That’s why it’s so important to:
👉 Always eat fruit whole, not juiced, dried, or smoothied.

This study shows that the best way to keep glucose stable is:

description:
You may have the idea that sorbet is healthier for you. This is a common belief! The reality is a bit different. While there are no published studies (that I’ve found) that compare the glucose curve of ice cream vs. sorbet in a lab setting, it’s easy to understand why sorbet leads to a bigger spike than ice cream when we look at their nutrition facts. 

👉 The ice cream and sorbet tested both have a similar amount of sugar in them: (24g for the ice cream, 23 for the sorbet, for 100g)
👉 BUT the ice cream also contains eggs and milk, while the sorbet doesn’t. The ice cream has 10 grams of fat, the sorbet only 2.5g. The ice cream has 5g of protein vs. 4g in the sorbet. Protein and fat reduce the spike of a food, because they don’t turn to glucose when digested and slow down glucose release. 

✅ In an ice cream, you’re “putting clothing on your carbs” with the big amount of fat and a bit more protein: steadier glucose curve. In a sorbet, it’s mostly sugar and water - naked carbs: bigger spike. 

 👉 The sorbet led to a bigger spike, and then a steeper crash.
👉 The ice cream kept glucose levels more steady.
🧠 We know that it’s the variability caused by spikes that is most damaging to our cells - so the spike and drop of the sorbet is worse from a glucose standpoint.

Interesting, right? But remember, ice cream or sorbet are there for pleasure! Eat the one you like the most.

To folllow up from yesterday’s Youtube episode on coffee - because I got so many questions about this: why do some people get a glucose spike from coffee and not others? 

The science isn’t clear yet, but here are some clues:
👉 In some people, coffee causes more of a stress response (you may feel anxious, agitated…), and in those bodies, it could lead to a glucose spike from the action of cortisol.

Where I’ve landed is the following: if you don’t feel anxious from drinking coffee, it probably doesn’t create a spike in your body. And the type of milk you choose and whether or not you put coffee in it has a MUCH bigger impact on its effect on your glucose levels! So, avoid sugar, and avoid sweetened nut milks or oat milk if you want a smaller spike. 

Thoughts? Let me know what you think.

description:
No! It’s not bad. Don’t worry it you see this on your glucose monitor. 

👉 High intensity exercise can make our liver release a bunch of glucose in our bloodstream to fuel our hard working muscles. That can show up on a glucose monitor as a spike! 

👉 More moderate activity like running usually doesn’t lead to those big spikes. 

But don’t worry- intense exercise induced spikes aren’t bad for us- the benefits of exercise far outweigh the short term inflammation from the spikes: when we exercise, our body doesn’t need insulin to uptake glucose. That is great! Second, the benifical effects of exercise on the body (reducing inflammation, improving insulin sensitivity, and positive impact on all systems of the body) outweigh the spike downsides.
--
¿El ejercicio intenso es malo para nuestra glucosa?

¡No! No es malo. No te preocupes si ves esto en tu medidor de glucosa. 

👉El ejercicio de alta intensidad puede hacer que el hígado libere una gran cantidad de glucosa en el torrente sanguíneo para alimentar los músculos. Esto puede aparecer en el medidor de glucosa como un pico. 

👉Una actividad más moderada, como correr, no suele provocar esos grandes picos. 

Pero no te preocupes: los picos intensos inducidos por el ejercicio no son malos para nosotros; los beneficios del ejercicio superan con creces la inflamación a corto plazo de los picos: cuando hacemos ejercicio, nuestro cuerpo no necesita insulina para captar glucosa. Eso es fantástico. En segundo lugar, los efectos beneficiosos del ejercicio en el organismo (reducción de la inflamación, mejora de la sensibilidad a la insulina e impacto positivo en todos los sistemas del organismo) superan los efectos negativos de los picos.

🕵️‍♀️ Many people believe that artificial sweeteners are worse for us than real sugar, because they are “artificial”. This is not true. For our bodies, these cause less harm than sugar. 

❗️But there are a few problems with artificial sweeteners: they may lead to us eating more sugar later (because I had a Caipirinha without sugar, I can have a cookie), they may hurt our gut microbiome, increase hunger or migraines.

👉 The bottom line: if you're trying to cut down on real sugar, sweeteners are a good option. Just try to limit them as well.

Should you drink during meals?

Studies have shown that the best way to keep glucose stable is:
👉 Do not drink water from 30 minutes before eating until the end of the meal.
👉 Why? Because drinking water during a meal high in carbohydrates and sugars can increase the glucose spike by up to 33%.

Be sure to drink plenty of water outside of meals.
In fact, being properly hydrated has many benefits:
👉 It is important for our overall health
👉 Helps eliminate excess glucose through urine
Both long-term and short-term studies show that drinking water reduces the risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

How much water should I drink?
👉 The recommended intake is around 2 liters per day.
👉 Ideally, you have to drink this amount of water during the day and not during meals.

👉 How to reconcile the vinegar and the water studies: have the vinegar drink 10minutes (or 30minutes if you can!) before the meal. Then during the meal don’t drink too much. Tada! ❤️

🧬 The study: « Drinking water with consumption of a jelly filled doughnut has a time dependent effect on the postprandiale blood glucose level in healthy young individuals » (2018)

👉 Honey is actually not a superior source of antioxidants. There are as many antioxidants in 1 tablespoon of honey as in 2 blueberries!
🙀 Honey is mostly sugar, and most commercial honeys aren't even honey at all.... they are just sugar syrup. 1 tablespoon of honey contains 18 grams of sugar, which is more than half the 30 grams recommended maximum amount of sugar per day for adults.
💙A better option to get antioxidants without the harmful side effects of sugar: have a blueberry. (or any other berries or whole fruit, or vegetables ❤️)

There is 5.15 mg/kg of flavonoid antioxidants in multi-floral honey. 1 tablespoon of honey is 21 grams. That gives 0.11mg of flavonoids per 1 tablespoons of honey.

description:
🍭 If we want to eat something sweet, like a cake or tropical fruit, it's better to do so after a meal than on an empty stomach.
⠀
💧 Our stomach is like a sink. When we eat sugar on an empty stomach, it goes straight to our intestine with nothing holding it back. This leads to a big, steep glucose spike.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
😇 If we already have some fiber, protein and fat in our stomach, anything sweet we eat after will be slowed down. This will keep our glucose levels much steadier and avoid a spike and a drop (potentially leading to more hunger) after. 
💞 Thank you @fatfueled23 for sharing this test!⠀
~~ ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍭 Si queremos comer algo dulce, como un pastel o una fruta tropical, es mejor hacerlo después de una comida y no con el estómago vacío.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
💧Nuestro estómago es como un fregadero. Cuando consumimos azúcar con el estómago vacío, va directo a nuestro intestino sin que nada lo frene. Esto lleva a un pico de glucemia abrupto y elevado. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
😇Si ya tenemos algo de fibra, proteína y grasa en nuestro estómago, cualquier cosa dulce que después comamos entrará más despacio. Esto mantendrá la concentración de glucosa más constante y evitará que luego haya picos y bajonas (las que generalmente dan más hambre). 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

¡Amantes del café! Esta publicación es para vosotros!

¿El café sube nuestros niveles de glucosa?

LA mayoría de las personas (especialmente con diabetes) experimentan un pequeño pico tras el café. Pero parece que varia mucho de una persona a otra, quizás por temas genéticos o por otros factores.

👉 Estos picos no parecen ser dañinos.

De hecho, en el largo plazo, tomar café está asociado con una salud mejor y con unos niveles de glucosa más saludables. Los científicos creen que sus beneficios se deben a los antioxidantes que el café contiene.

¿Porqué podemos tener un pico tras tomar café?

En el corto plazo,
👉La cafeína hace que nuestros músculos sean menos eficientes empapando la glucosa de nuestro torrente sanguíneo. 
👉La cafeína hace subir ciertas hormonas del estrés, como la adrenalina, que puede subir nuestros niveles de glucosa.
👉La cafeína hace que para nuestros cuerpos sea más difícil deshacerse del exceso de glucosa.

En el largo plazo, tomar café regularmente parece mejorar nuestros niveles de glucosa.

✨Consejos para el café✨

👉Es mejor tomar tu café después del desayuno, en lugar de antes del desayuno, especialmente si has tenido una noche en la que has dormido mal.

👉Evita beber café al mismo tiempo que una comida alta en azúcar o almidones, ya que puede empeorar el pico de glucosa.

👉Está bien añadir leche (de hecho, puede ayudar a mantener estable tu glucosa), pero ojo con añadir azúcar o nata, que a menudo contiene azúcar. Canela y cacao en polvo son opciones mejores.

They look different because they undergo different bleaching processes, or have extra molasses added to them. ​​​​​​​​
​​​​​​​​
A note on coconut sugar: The Philippines, a large producer of coconut sugar, released data claiming coconut sugar was healthier than regular sugar, and this was later proven to be wrong. Coconut sugar is the same as regular sugar.​​​​​​​​

👉 Our menstrual cycle impacts our glucose levels. In the two weeks before our period (the luteal phase), our glucose usually spikes higher for the same food. Scientists believe that this because sex hormones impact insulin sensitivity (how well you can dispose of glucose in your blood).
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
👉 What does this mean? That in our luteal phase, we will trigger glucose rollercoasters and cravings cycles more easily. It's even more important to use the hacks during this phase to feel our best.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🧬 "Fluctuations of Hyperglycemia and Insulin Sensitivity Are Linked to Menstrual Cycle Phases in Women With T1D" (2015)

💖 Adding vinegar (acetic acid) to our diet, either in a drink or as salad dressing, is an excellent way to flatten our glucose curves.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
👉Why? Because vinegar increases the speed at which our muscles soak up glucose after we eat. And when we flatten our glucose curves, we also reduce our risk of having cravings later.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
👉 1 tablespoon of vinegar (any kind – apple cider vinegar, white wine vinegar...) in a glass of water 1 to 10 minutes before meals (with a straw to protect our teeth)
👉 Some people have it before every meal, some just before they eat something sweet.
👉 ACV gummies don't work unfortunately.
👉 Pregnant women should avoid unpasturized apple cider vinegar. But pasteurized vinegars, like most of them, are safe.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
--
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
💖 Agregar vinagre a nuestra alimentación es una excelente manera de aplanar nuestras curvas de glucosa: en una bebida o a una salsa para ensalada. 
👉¿Por qué? Porque el vinagre aumenta la velocidad en la que nuestros músculos absorben la glucosa luego de comer. Y cuando aplanamos nuestras curvas de glucosa, reducimos las chances de tener antojos más tarde. 
👉1 cucharada de vinagre (cualquier tipo: vinagre de sidra de manzana, vinagre de vino blanco) en un vaso con agua de 1 a 10 minutos antes de una comida (con un popote o sorbete para proteger los dientes).
👉Algunas personas lo consumen antes de cualquier comida, y otras antes de comer algo dulce. 
👉Las gomitas y pastillas de VSM lamentablemente no funcionan.
👉Las mujeres embarazadas deberían evitar el vinagre de sidra de manzana sin pasteurizar. Pero la mayoría de los vinagres pasteurizados son seguros.

🕵️‍♀️ I often hear people say that they eat honey because it has antioxidants.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
👉 Honey is actually not a superior source of antioxidants. There are as many antioxidants in 1 tablespoon of honey as in 2 blueberries!
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🙀 Honey is mostly sugar, and most commercial honeys aren't even honey at all.... they are just sugar syrup. 1 tablespoon of honey contains 18 grams of sugar, which is more than half the 30 grams recommended maximum amount of sugar per day for adults. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
💙A better option to get antioxidants without the harmful side effects of sugar: have a blueberry. (or any other berries or whole fruit, or vegetables ❤️)
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🧬 Details: 
There is 5.15 mg/kg of flavonoid antioxidants in multi-floral honey. 1 tablespoon of honey is 21 grams. That gives 0.11mg of flavonoids per 1 tablespoons of honey. 
100 grams of blueberries contain on average 4mg of flavonoids. Two blueberries weigh 3 grams. That’s 0.12mg of flavonoids.

description:
💖 Adding vinegar (acetic acid) to our diet, either in a drink or as salad dressing, is an excellent way to flatten our glucose curves. 
👉Why? Because vinegar increases the speed at which our muscles soak up glucose after we eat. And when we flatten our glucose curves, we also reduce our risk of having cravings later. 
👉 1 tablespoon of vinegar (any kind – apple cider vinegar, white wine vinegar...) in a glass of water 1 to 10 minutes before meals (with a straw to protect our teeth)
👉 Some people have it before every meal, some just before they eat something sweet. 
👉 ACV gummies and pills don't work unfortunately.
👉 Pregnant women should avoid unpasteurized apple cider vinegar. But pasteurized vinegars, like most of them, are safe. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🧬Santos et al. "Vinegar (acetic acid) intake on glucose metabolism: A narrative review." Clinical nut ESPEN 32 (2019).
🧬Shishehbor et al. "Vinegar consumption can attenuate postprandial glucose...." Diab res 127 (2017).
-

Y cuando aplanamos nuestras curvas de glucosa, reducimos las chances de tener antojos más tarde. 👉1 cucharada de vinagre (cualquier tipo: vinagre de sidra de manzana, vinagre de vino blanco) en un vaso con agua de 1 a 10 minutos antes de una comida (con un popote o sorbete para proteger los dientes).👉Algunas personas lo consumen antes de cualquier comida, y otras antes de comer algo dulce. 👉Las gomitas y pastillas de VSM lamentablemente no funcionan.👉Las mujeres embarazadas deberían evitar el vinagre de sidra de manzana sin pasteurizar. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
✅ If we eat sweets after a meal, the food already in the stomach will slow down the glucose absorption.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
❓ Why are big glucose spikes bad for us? They hurt our cells, our mitochondria, and slowly contribute to our body aging. They also are more likely to lead to weight gain, mood swings, hunger and cravings.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🚩 And long term, too many glucose spikes can lead to type 2 diabetes and heart disease.

🍹Beware of cocktails… They can be sneaky sugar bombs. ⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍐 Alcoholic drinks with carbohydrate-rich mixers (e.g., fruit juices, simple syrup) can raise blood glucose, therefore increasing insulin in your system, and increasing your likelihood of fat gain. ⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍾 Alcohols that aren’t mixed with anything, like wine, whiskey, vodka, champagne, actually tend to decrease glucose levels. ⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
❓Why?⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
👉 Normally, the liver releases glucose to maintain blood sugar levels. But when alcohol is consumed, the liver is busy breaking the alcohol down, and it reduces its output of glucose into the bloodstream. ⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍷 This can lead to a drop in blood sugar levels if the alcohol was consumed on an empty stomach. ⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
📊 http://www.diabetes.org/food-and-fitness/food/what-can-i-eat/making-healthy-food-choices/alcohol.html⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
--⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍹Cuidado con los tragos. Pueden ser bombas de azúcar encubiertas.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍐Las bebidas alcohólicas con mezclas llenas de carbohidratos (por ejemplo, jugos de frutas o jarabes) pueden aumentar la glucosa en sangre y, entonces, elevar la insulina en tu sistema y las posibilidades de aumentar de peso.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍾De hecho, las bebidas alcohólicas que no tienen agregados, como el vino, whisky, vodka y el champán suelen disminuir la concentración glucémica.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
❓¿Por qué?⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
👉Por lo general, el hígado libera glucosa para mantener los niveles de azúcar en sangre. Pero cuando consumimos alcohol, el hígado está ocupado descomponiendo el alcohol y ya no puede producir la glucosa que va al torrente sanguíneo.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⁣⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
🍷 Esto puede causar una glucemia si el alcohol fue consumido con el estómago vacío. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

👉 Just adding cinnamon once on top of a meal will have no effect. ⁣⠀

👉 Cooled rice has a slightly lower glycemic response than freshly cooked white rice. ⁣⠀

🤔How is this possible? ⁣⠀
When starches are cooked and then cooled down, some of the starch turns into fibre (also called "resistant starch"). ⁣⠀
⁣⠀
🌀 Resistant starch is a carbohydrate that resist digestion in the small intestine and ferments in the large intestine. As the fibres ferment they act as a prebiotic and feed the good bacteria in the gut.⁣⠀
⁣⠀
🛶 Adding vinegar to something also reduces the glucose response. ⠀

⁣⠀
⁣⠀
⚠️ Most restaurants add sugar or sweetened rice wine (mirin) to sushi rice. The added sugar negates the effect of the resistant starch benefit from the cooled rice. In general, your glucose is better off if you order plain rice instead of sushi rice. ⠀
⠀

"Effect of cooling of cooked white rice on resistant starch content and glycemic response." (2015)⁣⠀
⁣⠀

🔰 A low glucose response can indicate either that Rennie’s GI tract didn’t let any glucose through to her blood (kinda cool for Rennie!) OR that she has so much circulating insulin that she instantly put the glucose away into her fat cells.⁣⠀

⁣⠀
🔅Insulin is the hormone that puts glucose AWAY into our cells after we’ve digested something that turns into glucose. ⁣The bigger an insulin response, the closer to metabolic disease.⁣⠀
⁣⠀
👉 Takeaway: use glucose data to compare two meals that YOU have had - but comparing across people is pretty much impossible.⁣⠀

⁣⠀
🍞 When starches are cooked and then cooled down, some of the starch turns into fibre (also called “resistant starch”). This fiber does not turn into glucose as it gets digested. ⁣⠀
⁣⠀
🧬 A fun test that demonstrates this (thanks @afridateran !) is looking at the glucose response of cooked vs. cooked-then-cooled starches. You’ll notice that the cooked-then-cooled starches turn into less glucose.

What’s better, fasted or not fasted? The scientific evidence is torn you guys. But the summary is: exercise is good for you, regardless. ⁣⠀

⁣⠀
🚩 These spikes aren’t to be avoided, they are just my body dumping stored glucose, which is good! ⁣⠀
⁣⠀
👉 When I ran post meal, my glucose levels in my blood were already high enough that my muscles could use the available glucose for energy. ⁣⠀
⁣⠀
♥️ Neither is good nor bad, they are just the result of different states when I exercise 😬⁣⠀

💘 My high glucose response could mean that I have very little circulating insulin (because I eat low carb most of the time), or that I have a ton of insulin but that there is no more place to put the glucose away. ⁣⠀
⁣⠀
👉 Takeaway: use glucose data to compare two meals that YOU have had - but comparing across people is pretty much impossible. ⁣⠀

⁣
♥️ Neither is good nor bad, they are just the result of different states when I exercise 😬⁣

🍹Beware of cocktails… They can be sneaky sugar bombs. ⁣
⁣
🍐 Alcoholic drinks with carbohydrate-rich mixers (e.g., fruit juices, simple syrup) can raise blood glucose, therefore increasing insulin in your system, and increasing your likelihood of fat gain. ⁣

⁣

description:
🤷‍♀️ When’s the best time to eat carbs for glucose control? (Spoiler alert: not on their own!) ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
🔬The amount of food left in your stomach impacts the glucose response of the next thing you eat.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
🥤🍊 Eating or drinking something high in carbs on an empty stomach will lead to a much bigger glucose spike than having the same thing following a meal.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⚙️Why is that? It’s potentially due to gastric emptying (aka how quickly food is moving from your stomach to your small intestine). ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
🚰 Think of it like a sink. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
🥤If the sink is empty and you pour orange juice into it, it’ll get through the drain really quickly.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
⛲️ If the sink is already full of water, orange juice you pour in will take a while to completely get through the drain, and it will be super diluted. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
👉 If you want to reduce glucose spikes (for example for less of a roller-coaster of energy levels throughout the day), eating carbs with other things instead of on their own can help you achieve that. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
#jambajuice #biohacking
